{{alias}}( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, PIV, RANK, TOL, WORK )
    Computes an unblocked Cholesky factorization with complete pivoting.

    Returns numeric INFO and writes RANK[0] separately. INFO=0 indicates
    complete factorization; INFO=1 indicates early termination from a
    cutoff or deficient/nonpositive remainder, not PSD certification.
    PIV contains the full positive 1-based permutation, including early
    termination. Incoming PIV/RANK contents are not input.

    The first positive maximum diagonal is accepted before testing TOL.
    Later candidates at or below the cutoff stop. Negative TOL requests
    N*2^-53*max(initial diagonal); nonnegative TOL is used directly.
    TOL is always required and must be a primitive finite number.

    Only the selected triangle changes; ignored storage/guards remain.
    WORK is mutable 2N output scratch. It remains unchanged if the initial
    maximum is nonpositive; otherwise its first half is zero-initialized
    and its second half stores candidate diagonals. Prior scratch values
    do not affect defined results. Finite selected inputs and finite
    intermediates define the reference-comparison domain.

    Active arrays require intrinsic ordinary ArrayBuffer backing.
    SharedArrayBuffer-backed views, including cloned shared storage, are
    rejected before writes. All four full indexed-byte envelopes must
    be disjoint. Disjoint subviews of one ordinary buffer are allowed.
    Externally aliased ordinary buffers from foreign addons are outside
    the caller contract. The matrix must be injective and full active
    views must fit; all indexing uses exact safe integers.

    Validation checks layout/uplo/N, finite primitive TOL, LDA, then RANK.
    For N=0, only RANK[0]=0 is written and INFO0 is returned. A/PIV/WORK
    are not accessed; inactive aliases may observe the rank byte write.
    This is package-defined empty behavior, not original-reference rank
    parity. Invalid types/selectors/backing throw TypeError; invalid
    geometry or nonfinite TOL throws RangeError before routine writes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string|number
        Row-major (101) or column-major (102) layout.

    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122) selected triangle.

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output full N-by-N matrix view.

    LDA: integer
        Matrix leading dimension, at least max(1,N), even when N=0.

    PIV: Int32Array
        Complete positive 1-based permutation output.

    RANK: Int32Array
        One active rank output scalar at index zero.

    TOL: number
        Required primitive finite tolerance; negative requests default.

    WORK: Float64Array
        Mutable 2N output scratch.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero on complete factorization or one on early termination.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 4, 0, 999, 1 ] );
    > var P = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 2 );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > var W = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 'upper', 2, A, 2, P, R, -1, W )
    0
    > R
    <Int32Array>[ 2 ]
    > P
    <Int32Array>[ 1, 2 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( uplo, N, A, r, c, oa, PIV, sp, op, RANK, or, TOL, W, sw, ow )
    Computes the factorization using explicit element strides/offsets.

    The matrix is A[oa+i*r+j*c], permutation PIV[op+i*sp], rank RANK[or],
    and scratch W[ow+i*sw]. Positive and negative strides are supported;
    mutable broadcasts with extent greater than one are rejected.
    All scalar, backing, envelope, and finite-domain rules above apply.

    For N=0 validate uplo/N, required primitive finite TOL and active
    RANK/or; write only RANK[or]=0 and return INFO0. A/PIV/W and unused
    strides/offsets are not inspected. Inactive aliases can observe that
    scalar write. This is new package behavior, not reference rank parity.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uplo: string|number
        Upper (121) or lower (122) selected triangle.

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    A: Float64Array
        Full input/output N-by-N matrix.

    r: integer
        Matrix row stride.

    c: integer
        Matrix column stride.

    oa: integer
        Matrix starting index.

    PIV: Int32Array
        Complete positive 1-based permutation output.

    sp: integer
        Permutation stride.

    op: integer
        Permutation starting index.

    RANK: Int32Array
        Active output scalar buffer.

    or: integer
        Index of the active rank scalar.

    TOL: number
        Required primitive finite tolerance.

    W: Float64Array
        Mutable 2N output scratch.

    sw: integer
        Scratch stride.

    ow: integer
        Scratch starting index.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero or one.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 4 ] );
    > var P = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > var R = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > var W = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'lower', 1, A, 1, 1, 0, P, 1, 0, R, 0, 100, W, 1, 0 )
    0
    > R
    <Int32Array>[ 1 ]
    > A
    <Float64Array>[ 2 ]

    See Also
    --------
